node.build: Official 11.2.0 Linux amd64 release asset; SHA256 8b287e300ffb2063522fc33d50da6ecee8fa10fc7445c906fae0ca9783db8e03 (GitHub marks this tag as a prerelease).

run.cli: cardano-cli 11.6.0.0 from the same release archive
setup: One stake pool, three DReps, no constitutional committee, testnet magic 42, 200-slot epochs of 0.1 s, generated with cardano-testnet create-env.

ExperimentalHardForksEnabled and TestDijkstraHardForkAtEpoch 2 in the generated versioned configuration. The epoch trigger changes the era but initially leaves protocol version 10. Two governance actions raised it to 11 then 12.

The recorded transaction matrix was rerun after checking protocol version 12; earlier pre-PV12 trial output is excluded. Live slots, hashes, keys, timing, transaction inclusion and build resolution are not deterministic.

Ogmios and Kupo first rejected the versioned configuration envelope. Their subsequent protocol checks use an equivalent flattened legacy configuration. db-sync also needs Protocol and LastKnownBlockVersion fields plus a Shelley genesis copy rounded to Byron whole-second startTime (under one second difference).

Version labels identify exactly what ran: current releases and Pallas main are checked alongside historical gouroboros, txtop and cardano-node-api controls. The locally patched tool builds are experiments, not upstream releases.

The codec matrix retains 17 transaction encodings (9 signed envelopes, including a rejected legacy certificate, plus 8 mempool encodings), 168 raw Dijkstra blocks, and a Conway block as a positive CML control. HFC framing is added only for the CML MultiEraBlock probe.
Raw logs, fixtures, resolved build inputs and checksums are retained under content/readiness/dijkstra-runs/2026-11-01/. No signing keys or credentials are retained.
Koios and advanced Dijkstra transaction bodies (nested transactions, direct deposits, balance intervals, PlutusV4) were not executed. Pass means only the capability and cases named by that check.

checks.title: Which Conway-built transactions the node accepts after the fork

The eight captured mempool encodings have three elements and retain the signed-envelope transaction ids. This checks submission and encoding; it is not full coverage of every guard or removed encoding.
